prompt.context: Your client is interested in opening a manufacturing plant for spark plugs in Spain.
prompt.question: How would you advise them? Should they open the manufacturing plant?

clarifying_info.q: What types of spark plug applications should we consider?
clarifying_info.a: Mention other uses (trucks, lawn-mowers, diesel engines, etc.) but focus on the passenger car consumer market for simplicity.

clarifying_info.q: Should we consider corporate fleet or truck demand?
clarifying_info.a: No — ignore fleet and truck markets; focus only on the consumer passenger car market.

clarifying_info.q: What raw materials are needed for spark plugs?
clarifying_info.a: Probe the interviewer — steel, ceramics, copper for electrodes; typical manufacturing inputs.

framework: 1. Market Sizing — estimate annual Spanish spark plug demand (guesstimation): population → households → cars per household → new cars per year + replacement demand from existing fleet; account for cylinders per car and economic life of spark plugs
2. Market Attractiveness — Porter's Five Forces: supplier power, buyer power, barriers to entry, threat of substitutes, competitive rivalry

3. Country Attractiveness — Porter's Diamond: factor conditions (wages, raw materials proximity), demand conditions (domestic market size), related/supporting industries, firm strategy/rivalry/structure; also consider market isolation of Spain
4. Cost Structure & Order-Winning Criteria — raw materials, labor, transportation, margin; understand how auto OEM contracts are won
5. Recommendation — synthesize market size, competitive dynamics, and country advantages/disadvantages into a go/no-go recommendation with risks and next steps

questions.prompt: Estimate the annual demand for spark plugs in the Spanish passenger car market.
questions.guidance: Strong answer walks through: Population 36M → ~12M households (3 per household) → assume ~0.8–1 car per household → ~10–12M cars in stock. New car demand: assume average economic life of 10 years → ~1–1.2M new cars/year. Each car has 4–8 cylinders (assume average 4–6), one spark plug per cylinder. New car demand: 1M cars × 5 plugs = 5M plugs/year. Replacement demand: spark plugs changed every ~30,000 miles or ~3 years; 10M cars ÷ 3 = ~3.3M replacement sets/year × 5 plugs = ~16.5M plugs/year. Total ≈ 20–25M spark plugs per year. Candidate should state assumptions clearly and sanity-check the result.

math.setup: Estimate annual spark plug demand: new car demand + replacement demand
steps: Assume 0.8–1 car per household → ~10M cars in stock
New cars per year: economic life = 10 years → 10M ÷ 10 = 1M new cars/year
Average cylinders per car = 5 (mix of 4- and 6-cylinder), 1 plug per cylinder
Replacement interval ≈ every 3 years → 10M cars ÷ 3 ≈ 3.3M replacement sets/year

questions.prompt: Analyze the competitive landscape using Porter's Five Forces.
questions.guidance: Supplier power: steel, ceramics, copper are commodity inputs — low-to-moderate supplier power. Buyer power: OEM auto manufacturers are large, concentrated buyers with high switching leverage — high buyer power. Barriers to entry: capital-intensive manufacturing, OEM certification requirements, incumbent scale — moderate-to-high barriers. Threat of substitutes: electric vehicles eventually replace combustion engines and eliminate spark plug demand — growing long-term threat. Competitive rivalry: global incumbents (NGK, Bosch, Champion, Denso) dominate with scale; intense rivalry — high.

questions.prompt: Assess Spain's attractiveness as a manufacturing location using Porter's Diamond.
questions.guidance: Factor conditions: relatively lower labor costs vs. Northern Europe, proximity to automotive OEM plants in Spain (SEAT/VW, Renault, Ford); raw material access depends on local mining/ceramics industry. Demand conditions: Spain has a significant domestic car market; also well-placed for export to Europe. Related and supporting industries: established auto components ecosystem in Spain. Firm strategy/rivalry: local competition may be limited — potential first-mover advantage. Also consider geographic market isolation providing some protection.

questions.prompt: What are the key cost components and order-winning criteria for winning OEM contracts?
questions.guidance: Cost components: raw materials (steel/ceramics/copper), labor, energy, transportation, overhead/margin. Order-winning criteria for auto OEM contracts: consistent quality/reliability, JIT delivery capability, competitive price, certification to OEM specs, long-term supply relationship. Candidate should link cost structure to Spain's factor conditions (e.g., lower labor costs help if labor is a significant cost driver).

brainstorming.prompt: What other factors should the client consider before making a final go/no-go decision on the manufacturing plant?

categories.name: Market & Demand Risks
ideas: Long-term shift to electric vehicles reduces spark plug demand
Demand concentration risk if a few OEMs represent most revenue
Cyclicality of auto manufacturing affecting volume

categories.name: Operational & Supply Chain
ideas: Reliability of raw material supply chains in Spain
Manufacturing technology requirements and capital expenditure
Lead time to achieve OEM certification and quality standards
Logistics cost to serve rest of European market

categories.name: Competitive & Strategic
ideas: Response from global incumbents (NGK, Bosch, Denso) — possible price war
Ability to differentiate on quality or service vs. established players
Partnership or JV with a local manufacturer vs. greenfield build

categories.name: Financial & Regulatory
ideas: Required investment level vs. projected returns
EU labor regulations and environmental compliance costs
Available government incentives for manufacturing investment in Spain
Currency risk if inputs are priced in USD but revenues in EUR

recommendation: Conditionally proceed if market sizing confirms ~20–25M units/year demand and Spain's cost advantages (lower labor, OEM proximity, potential market isolation) yield a competitive cost position
Prioritize securing anchor OEM contracts before committing to full plant build — validate buyer willingness to switch suppliers
risks: Long-term structural decline in spark plug demand from EV transition
High buyer concentration gives OEMs leverage to compress margins
Entrenched global competitors may respond aggressively on price
next_steps: Conduct detailed OEM demand interviews to validate annual volume and contract terms
Model full business case: capex, operating costs, break-even volume, IRR
Assess EV penetration trajectory in Spain to bound demand outlook
Evaluate alternative entry modes (acquisition of existing plant, JV) to reduce risk and accelerate OEM certification
